Y., March 28, ’77. <sentence_start/>Dr. Up de Graff : I have been an attentive reader of your valua- ble Bistoury for some years, and seeing you receive correspondence from many persons afflict- ed with disease, I concluded you would notice my short letter. <sentence_start/>1 was burned some six or seven years ago by an explosion of powder, which left some red scars about my face, which I would give most any price to have removed. <sentence_start/>If you could give me any advice or send me any receipt for their remov- al, I would pay you your price willingly. <sentence_start/>C. <sentence_start/>If th# scars are broad and red, they can be re- moved surgically, and new skin transplanted. <sentence_start/>If not very large, had better let them alone. <sentence_start/>Nashville, Tenn., April 18, 1877. <sentence_start/>Dr. Up de Graff : My father has what I suppose to be cataract. <sentence_start/>He is seventy-one years old, and his sight has been gradually failing him for three years. <sentence_start/>He is now entirely blind in his right eye and nearly so in his left. <sentence_start/>Can he have his right eye operated upon now, or must he wait until he is blind in his left one, and have both done at once? <sentence_start/>Can we come at any time to have the operation performed, or should we select cold weather as the best time ? <sentence_start/>J. R. B. <sentence_start/>He can have the blind eye operated upon at any time-need not wait for .the second one to become blind. <sentence_start/>The operation can also be done at any sea- son of the year that suits your convenience. <sentence_start/>Green, N. Y., 4, 29, 1877. <sentence_start/>Dr. Up de Graff : Dear Sir:--I admire a forehead with an open spade between the eyebrows, and would know is there a harmless recipe for removing the hair and trimming the eyebrows. <sentence_start/>Will pulling out the hair for a number of times have the desired effect ? <sentence_start/>C. T. B. <sentence_start/>Pulling out the hairs will not prevent their re- growing. <sentence_start/>See back numbers of the Bistoury for a depilatory that will answer your purpose. <sentence_start/>Jackson, Mich., May 7th, 1877. <sentence_start/>Dr. Up de Graff : Our little boy, aged four, has a rupture. <sentence_start/>The tumor seems to grow larger. <sentence_start/>Is there anything we can do to stop it ? <sentence_start/>P. R. <sentence_start/>Construct a snug-fitting bandage, to go about his waist, with gores cut to fit the top of the hips. <sentence_start/>Take an old elastic suspender, cut two pieces from it, each two or three inches long. <sentence_start/>Sew them to each end of a padded band, long enough to reach between the legs and "button snugly upon the waist-band, front and rear. <sentence_start/>To the band passing between the limbs, fasten a smooth rubber button, as large as half of a black walnut. <sentence_start/>Let this rest immediately over the opening in the abdomen through which the intestine is found to protrude. <sentence_start/>This will hold the hernia in place, and if worn faithfully for a year, is likely to cure the boy. <sentence_start/>Better have your family physician apply the band- age and advise you in its construction. <sentence_start/>Frankfort, Ky., May 17th, 1877. <sentence_start/>Editor Bistoury: What can I do for my little boy, six years of age, who is suffering from paralysis of both legs ? <sentence_start/>He can stand alone but cannot walk. <sentence_start/>Mrs. L. Cannot tell without knowing more about the case. <sentence_start/>See last number of the Bistoury for full information upon this subject. <sentence_start/>Owatonna, Minn., June 1st, 1877. <sentence_start/>Dr. Thad S. Up de Graff : Have read the Bistoury for many years, have been interested and entertained by it, but now am forced to seek its advice. <sentence_start/>Have been using iny eyes considerably lately in reading, particularly in the evening, to entertain an invalid mother. <sentence_start/>I am now troubled with sensitiveness to light, with bright and dark specks floating before my eyes. <sentence_start/>Now and then pain is felt in the eyes and over the brow. <sentence_start/>They are growing worse, so that it is now difficult for me to read at all. <sentence_start/>What can I do for (hem ? ■ Mrs. J. D. Stop reading, writing, sewing or other work in which the eyes are employed. <sentence_start/>Give your eyes absolute and complete rest. <sentence_start/>Bathe the closed eye- lids in cold water several times daily. <sentence_start/>Keep cool and quiet. <sentence_start/>If the unpleasant symptoms do not speedily disappear, consult an oculist. <sentence_start/>You are suffering from congestion of the retina, brought on by over-use of the eyes. <sentence_start/>Tuscaloosa, Ala., June 1st, 1877. <sentence_start/>Dr. Up de Graff : Where can I procure one of Dr. Knapp’s oph- thalmoscopes ? .
